objective: Implement the designed production session rules on the accepted opposition slice: three destroyed pylons unlock extraction, extraction wins, and player death or the 150-second deadline loses.
completion_contract: Outcome: in ai-game-05, extend the existing session rather than replacing accepted systems. Consume once-only destructible-target events, count distinct destroyed pylons, reject extraction until all three are destroyed, and require entry into the existing 1.5m extraction radius to win. Enforce the designed 150-second active-play deadline and resolve terminal outcomes after gameplay damage with loss-before-win precedence. Pause stops the session clock; terminal resolution is idempotent. Preserve normal combat, physical fragment bursts, and sound. Evidence: committed and pushed source, focused automated tests, actual Godot execution logs, and reproduction commands tied to the source revision. Tests cover duplicate destruction signals, locked extraction, unlock and victory, death, timeout boundaries, same-tick loss versus victory, pause, and terminal idempotency. Validation: independently rerun tests and inspect production event wiring and processing order. Clearly distinguish isolated rule fixtures from natural gameplay; do not claim this child establishes full-session playability or subjective quality.
state_memo: completed: contract validated against referenced artifacts

objective: Integrate the accepted complete session as the default Linux game, with objective/status feedback and reliable restart after victory or defeat.
completion_contract: Prerequisite: the session-rules child is independently accepted. Outcome: default project launch enters the complete game rather than controls-only mode. Using the existing visual/audio direction, show controls, the destroy-three-pylons-then-extract objective, pylon progress, locked/open extraction status, remaining time, health and dash status, pause state, and explicit victory/defeat results with retry instructions. Extend the existing restart boundary, not a parallel implementation. Retry fully restores health, clock, objectives, pylons, extraction lock, player/input state, and opposition, while clearing prior bolts, debris, and sound voices. Evidence: committed and pushed integration source and automated launch, HUD-binding, pause/resume, and repeated win/loss/restart tests; fresh rendered Linux captures with code-level pixel checks and engine logs. Validation: independently launch the default entry and rerun tests, checking that the production scene includes combat, destruction, sound, and opposition and that repeated resets leave no stale state or duplicate callbacks. Forced terminal fixtures may test reset boundaries but must be labeled as fixtures, not natural victories. Subjective readability remains for node 9.
